title: Glider
statementMd:
A plane is flying at a constant height of $h$ meters above the ground surface. Let's consider that it is flying from the point $(-10^9, h)$ to the point $(10^9, h)$ parallel with $Ox$ axis.

A glider is inside the plane, ready to start his flight at any moment (for the sake of simplicity let's consider that he may start only when the plane's coordinates are integers). After jumping from the plane, he will fly in the same direction as the plane, parallel to $Ox$ axis, covering a unit of distance every second. Naturally, he will also descend; thus his second coordinate will decrease by one unit every second.

There are ascending air flows on certain segments, each such segment is characterized by two numbers $x_1$ and $x_2$ ($x_1 \lt x_2$) representing its endpoints. No two segments share any common points. When the glider is inside one of such segments, he doesn't descend, so his second coordinate stays the same each second. The glider still flies along $Ox$ axis, covering one unit of distance every second.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/48923c71b04bf225eb34940d72bd23858ba6d97b.png) If the glider jumps out at $1$, he will stop at $10$. Otherwise, if he jumps out at $2$, he will stop at $12$.

Determine the maximum distance along $Ox$ axis from the point where the glider's flight starts to the point where his flight ends if the glider can choose any integer coordinate to jump from the plane and start his flight. After touching the ground the glider stops altogether, so he cannot glide through an ascending airflow segment if his second coordinate is $0$.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $h$ $(1 \le n \le 2\cdot10^{5}, 1 \le h \le 10^{9})$ — the number of ascending air flow segments and the altitude at which the plane is flying, respectively.

Each of the next $n$ lines contains two integers $x_{i1}$ and $x_{i2}$ $(1 \le x_{i1} \lt x_{i2} \le 10^{9})$ — the endpoints of the $i$-th ascending air flow segment. No two segments intersect, and they are given in ascending order.

## Output

Print one integer — the maximum distance along $Ox$ axis that the glider can fly from the point where he jumps off the plane to the point where he lands if he can start his flight at any integer coordinate.

## Note

In the first example if the glider can jump out at $(2, 4)$, then the landing point is $(12, 0)$, so the distance is $12-2 = 10$.

In the second example the glider can fly from $(16,10)$ to $(34,0)$, and the distance is $34-16=18$.

In the third example the glider can fly from $(-100,1000000000)$ to $(1999999899,0)$, so the distance is $1999999899-(-100)=1999999999$.
statementZhMd:
一架飞机以距地面 $h$ 米的恒定高度飞行。设它沿平行于 $Ox$ 轴的方向，从点 $(-10^9, h)$ 飞往点 $(10^9, h)$。

一名滑翔员在飞机内，随时准备开始自己的飞行（为简化问题，假设他只能在飞机坐标为整数时起飞）。从飞机上跳下后，他将沿与飞机相同的方向、平行于 $Ox$ 轴飞行，每秒前进一个单位的距离。同时，他也会下降，因此他的第二坐标每秒减少一个单位。

在某些线段上存在上升气流，每条线段由两个数 $x_1$ 和 $x_2$（$x_1 \lt x_2$）表示其端点。任意两条线段没有公共点。当滑翔员位于其中一条线段内时，他不会下降，因此他的第二坐标每秒保持不变。滑翔员仍然沿 $Ox$ 轴飞行，每秒前进一个单位的距离。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/48923c71b04bf225eb34940d72bd23858ba6d97b.png) 如果滑翔员在 $1$ 处跳下，他将在 $10$ 处停止。否则，如果他在 $2$ 处跳下，他将在 $12$ 处停止。

请确定滑翔员从开始飞行的位置到结束飞行的位置之间沿 $Ox$ 轴的最大距离，其中滑翔员可以选择从飞机上的任意整数坐标处跳下并开始飞行。滑翔员接触地面后会立即完全停止，因此当他的第二坐标为 $0$ 时，他无法飞过上升气流线段。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $n$ 和 $h$（$1 \le n \le 2\cdot10^{5}, 1 \le h \le 10^{9}$）——上升气流线段的数量以及飞机飞行的高度。

接下来的 $n$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $x_{i1}$ 和 $x_{i2}$（$1 \le x_{i1} \lt x_{i2} \le 10^{9}$）——第 $i$ 条上升气流线段的端点。任意两条线段不相交，且它们按照递增顺序给出。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——如果滑翔员可以从任意整数坐标处开始飞行，他从跳下飞机的位置到着陆位置之间沿 $Ox$ 轴能够飞行的最大距离。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，如果滑翔员可以在 $(2, 4)$ 处跳下，那么着陆点为 $(12, 0)$，因此距离为 $12-2 = 10$。

在第二个样例中，滑翔员可以从 $(16,10)$ 飞到 $(34,0)$，因此距离为 $34-16=18$。

在第三个样例中，滑翔员可以从 $(-100,1000000000)$ 飞到 $(1999999899,0)$，因此距离为 $1999999899-(-100)=1999999999$。
